text:
Maya: Heads-up — Console is showing 'rate cap exceeded' for proj-finance but raw gateway logs have requests attributed to a service account owned by org-infra. Anyone else hitting this?
Sam: Yep saw a few alerts earlier. Looks like enforcement is charging the key owner rather than the caller @Ravi — expected?
Ravi: That's by-design from the earlier token-exchange change: quota enforcement uses the key's billing_project when present. origin_project was only used for UI visibility at the time.
Jon: From product/customer perspective that will confuse billing teams. They expect the initiating project to be charged in most cases, not the key-holding org. We should show both at minimum.
Maya: Minimal repro: header snapshot 
```
Authorization: Bearer sa-key-123
X-Forwarded-Project: proj-finance-9
X-Impersonated-By: service-account@org-infra
```
Logs show: billing_project=org-infra-billing, caller=proj-finance-9
Sam: Telemetry problem — traces only have billing_project so when CS investigates they see charges but no caller context. Makes troubleshooting impossible.
Ravi: Two paths here: (A) change enforcement to prefer origin_project when present (breaking behavior for some orgs), or (B) keep enforcement as-is but change telemetry + console to surface both 'Charged to' and 'Caller' clearly.
Jon: Product prefers B for rollout speed, but wants an opt-in flag for some orgs to flip enforcement to origin_project for legacy billing setups.
Maya: Edge case: delegated service account exchanges where origin_project header is missing — enforcement must have a deterministic fallback, otherwise we risk denying traffic.
Sam: Also consider where enforcement happens — edge (gateway) vs central rate service. If we rely on header we must trust the hop that sets it; need signed origin assertions or risk spoofing.
Ravi: Proposal: add two request attributes at gateway: `billing_affinity` with values [key_owner|origin_project|delegated_project] and `effective_billing_project` which is the resolved project id. Record both in traces and in per-request audit entry.
Jon: For console/UX: route dashboard -> per-route breakdown columns = [Charged to, Caller project, Impersonated-by]. Small tooltip = precedence rules + opt-in flag. Also show a toggle: "Show effective billing" that switches chart aggregation.
Maya: Can we also add an audit event for enforcement decision so CS can export a CSV when customers dispute charges?
Sam: Audit per-request is expensive. Suggest sampling: 1% baseline + full capture on enforcement_reject or when user flags a dispute. Also keep aggregated counters at high cardinality for 30d.
Ravi: Agreed. Migration: we should run a 30d shadow mode where we emit the `effective_billing_project` based on new precedence rules but not actually enforce. Compare diffs before any live flip.
Jon: Action items: Ravi -> draft header spec + precedence table; Maya -> console mockups for both view modes; Sam -> telemetry/sampling proposal & cost estimate; Ops-bot -> enable 30d shadow mode flag in staging. Target: RFC and mock review by next Tue.
Maya: I'll open the RFC draft and attach mock images. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
